proof-narrative-lean-equiv.evidence: Lean (sibling) `atomicMassGBNF` is a `def` (m_e·ρ_K· | tr_M(NF_GS β) | ): the claimed formula is the definition, nothing asserted. With ρ_K a free positive scalar the statement is contentless: for any mass m and any braid with tr ≠ 0, ρ_K := m/(m_e | tr | ) works. tr_M(NF_GS(B)) = tr_M(B) holds trivially, since the normal form is the same element of H_n. The Lean docstring itself cites a 22–31 % empirical gap for ρ_K

[full review 2026-11-21; scope note rewritten 2026-11-19, 48f446490cc] The Lean is unchanged: atomicMassGBNF is a def equal to the formula, so nothing is asserted, and rho_K is still a free positive scalar. The 2026-11-15 scope note said honestly that the relation 'fixes nothing: any mass is reproduced by choosing rho_K', and that the definition of rho_K is open. The new note replaces this with a claim that the relation 'acquires predictive content' once rho_K is specified through the graded expansion prop:rho-k-graded-expansion (mass-theory/rho-k-graded-expansion.md). That block does not support the claim. (1) It is downstream of this one: it is obtained 'by multiplying the GB-NF identity through', so using it to give this identity content is circular. (2) Its own scope note says only the leading piece is proved, and that piece puts the nucleon and electron masses in by mass additivity. The single-generator piece has a prefactor 'chosen against the mass table', which is a fit under the no-fitting ruling, and the pair-generator piece is open. So rho_K is still not specified independently of m(K), and the old wording was the accurate one. Also the reference is a raw \ref{prop:rho-k-graded-expansion} rather than a link, and the block is not in uses[].

Re-read at 68ebfb21a05: the Lean (atomicMassGBNF, a def equal to the formula) is unchanged and #8889 only relabels B_K. Earlier 2026-11-21 verdict stands: the def asserts nothing, rho_K is a free positive scalar, and the scope note's claim that the relation 'acquires predictive content' via prop:rho-k-graded-expansion is circular (that block is downstream) and not in uses[].

da-definitional-ambiguity.evidence: Read of the edited statement at 68ebfb21a05.
da-definitional-ambiguity.notes: Two strand counts in one sentence: B_K lives in H_{3A}(q) (three quark strands per nucleon) and is called 'the electron-free core of the atomic braid A in H_{A+Z}(q)'. Since 3A > A+Z for every atom, B_K is not a sub-word of A, so 'core of A' needs a stated map (e.g. a cabling of the A nucleon strands into 3A quark strands). The closing phrase still calls rho_K 'the categorical density of the atomic braid class' after the relabel to a Hecke word. Pre-existing; #8889 makes it more visible but does not introduce it.
